matches.quote: the Discussion's "Our experiments confirm the long-standing question" and the abstract's "direct evidence of TRSB" overstate what is shown
The authors should show raw IV curves at zero and a few other fields for both polarities, with the sweep order reversed
The in-plane-field bistability has conventional explanations that are not excluded... discuss what pins the domain configuration.
Ring 1 has positive ΔIc at zero field (Fig. 2b) and Ring 2 negative (Fig. 2c).
The remanent-field correction in Eq. 1 is ambiguous and may absorb or distort the reported asymmetry
In Ring 2 (Fig. 2c), ΔIc is a nearly field-independent negative offset of about 5-8 µA on Ic of 60-140 µA at all three temperatures
apply the ΔIc analysis of Fig. 2b,c, with an identical protocol... to at least one device where TRSB should be absent
In Ring 2, ΔIc stays at about -5 to -8 µA at 400, 800 and 1000 mK while Ic roughly doubles, so ΔIc/Ic falls on cooling.
cites "Figure 1d" for the IV curves under RF (they are in 1c) and "Figure 1e" for the power dependence (that is 1d; there is no 1e).
The authors should show ΔIc(T), ΔIc/Ic and the zero-field diode efficiency from base temperature to Tc for each ring
The authors should discuss the junction IcRn and its temperature dependence (Ambegaokar-Baratoff or KO-type against phase-slip behaviour)
The sign of ΔIc and of the zero-field diode should then be random across zero-field thermal cycles (or set by pinning)

notes: C12 asks to eliminate domain walls (e.g. monodomain state by high field/field cooling or a geometry without walls) and show the effects vanish; P21 asks for null controls on geometries/phases without domain walls (e.g. Ring 2 disk stage or 3K-phase rings) and P5 asks for field cooling, so C12 is marked 'partly'. C6 asks for rectification coefficient vs field and T; P6 and P17 ask for diode efficiency (ΔIc/Ic) vs T, so C6 is marked 'partly'. C18 asks for the physical origin of the current-switchable bistability; P16 proposes conventional mechanisms (JxB vortex forces, fluxoid states, fluxon switching) and asks what pins the domains while P10 suggests TDGL modelling with bias current and in-plane field, so C18 is marked 'partly'.
